topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Framing
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture by framing cancer development as an evolutionary process shaped by genetic alterations, cell of origin, and the microenvironment.

topics.label: Genetic and Epigenetic Drivers of Clonal Evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how Darwinian clonal selection is driven by both sequential genetic mutations and alterations in the epigenetic transcriptional landscape.

topics.label: Cell of Origin and the Cancer Stem Cell Model
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the cancer stem cell model and examine experimental evidence for stem cell hierarchy and cell of origin across leukemia and colorectal cancers.

topics.label: Inflammatory Promotion and Microenvironmental Triggering of Tumorigenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics demonstrate how environmental promoters and chronic inflammation cooperate with driver mutations to trigger stem-like states and drive malignant transformation.

topics.label: Microenvironmental Codependency, Spatial Profiling, and Coevolutionary Synthesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the dependence of established tumors on stromal interactions, the spatial methods used to profile them, and an overarching synthesis of tumor-microenvironment coevolution.

topics.label: Closing Remarks and Preview of Next Lecture
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture and previews the upcoming session on cancer therapies.
